audit_findings.title: Owner earnings and diluted units represent different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.387 million difference between 2025 consolidated net income of $99.651 million and parent-attributable net income of $86.264 million; 13.807606 million Class B/OpCo units; excluding those units from 141.667 million increases per-unit value by 10.8%
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator reflects the parent claim while the diluted-share denominator includes units sharing in whole-OpCo earnings, depressing value per common unit.
audit_findings.evidence: The Partnership’s Class B units are exchangeable on a one-for-one basis, together with an equal number of OpCo common units, for common units of the Partnership.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated basis mismatch. A denominator-only correction would raise the reported $6.22-$9.51 range to approximately $6.89-$10.54. A whole-OpCo numerator correction could differ because taxes and claim-specific charges must also be rebuilt. The correction is material to the stated valuation even though the denominator-only result remains below the $14.88 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun either with 13.807606 million Class B/OpCo units removed from the denominator or with OE rebuilt on a fully converted whole-OpCo basis, including consistent taxes and claim adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Series A redemption economics may be missing
audit_findings.magnitude: $191.100 million redemption value at June 30, 2026, computed as 162,500 units multiplied by $1,176; 10.783 million if-converted units included
audit_findings.mechanism: If conversion conditions were unmet, the preferred redemption claim must be deducted in the equity bridge and its conversion shares excluded rather than treated as common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The Series A preferred units rank senior to the Partnership’s common units with respect to distribution rights and rights upon liquidation.
audit_findings.explanation: At $14.88, the common-unit price was below the holder-conversion threshold of 130% of $15.07, or $19.591. Substituting the filed redemption claim for the 10.783 million conversion shares would produce approximately $5.27, $7.32 and $8.84 per share for bear, base and bull, versus $6.22, $8.11 and $9.51. This does not reverse the current market-price conclusion by itself, but it materially changes common-equity values and is a demonstrated claim-treatment problem unless another conversion basis applies.
audit_findings.action: Verify conversion eligibility on September 6, 2026 and whether OE already bears preferred distributions or accretion; if ineligible, deduct the current redemption value and accrued distributions and remove the 10.783 million shares.

audit_findings.title: The Dropdown perimeter check is past due
audit_findings.magnitude: $75.0 million cash plus 9.5 million OpCo units and 9.5 million corresponding Class B units; the new units equal 6.7% of the 141.667 million valuation denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would change the operating-earnings perimeter and potentially cash, debt, preferred claims and diluted units used in the equity bridge and per-share calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: We may decide to fund any acquisition, including any potential dropdowns, with cash, common units, other equity securities, proceeds from borrowings under our secured revolving credit facility or the issuance of debt securities, or any combination thereof.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation date is after its August 21, 2026 rerun trigger, but the supplied record establishes only an expected closing. The financing and issued-unit amounts are large enough to affect the valuation materially, while acquired OE and actual post-closing debt are unavailable. Direction is mixed because acquired earnings add value while cash consideration, financing costs and dilution reduce it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing 8-K or other filed confirmation and rerun with final consideration, financing, issued securities, acquired earnings and post-closing balance-sheet amounts; document delay or termination if it did not close.

audit_findings.title: Reserve replacement may be an omitted maintenance cost
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed average five-year PDP decline rate: 13.5%)
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back depletion without deducting the economic reinvestment needed to sustain reserves can overstate OE, positive growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: To the extent that we do not withhold replacement capital expenditures, a portion of our cash available for distribution will represent a return of your capital.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is not demonstrated because the exact OE bridge and sustaining-reinvestment requirement are absent. It is nevertheless reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation: existing PDP production has a filed 13.5% average decline rate, while the DCF assumes positive growth and a perpetual terminal value. Operator-funded development may offset some depletion, but the record does not establish that it supports the modeled growth without recurring acquisitions.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $78.6 million anchor's treatment of depletion and acquisitions, then estimate sustaining reinvestment from reserve and production roll-forwards, organic reserve additions and recurring acquisition economics before rerunning growth and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Full conversion changes the tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (13.807606 million Class B/OpCo units affected; 21% federal statutory rate)
audit_findings.mechanism: A whole-OpCo OE numerator paired with fully exchanged units requires corporate-level tax on income formerly allocated to tax-exempt noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.evidence: The non-controlling interest, which is held by the OpCo common unitholders, is not subject to federal income taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is conditional on correcting the first finding through a whole-OpCo gross-up rather than removing the minority units. The filing demonstrates that noncontrolling-interest income currently escapes parent-level federal tax, but depletion deductions, the valuation allowance and post-exchange taxable income prevent a reliable tax amount from the supplied record. It could partially reverse the value uplift from grossing up OE, but materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a pro-forma post-exchange tax calculation using the same ownership basis as the diluted denominator, including depletion, interest limitations, state taxes and the valuation allowance, and rerun OE after cash taxes.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may contain unrealized derivative income
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.227 million unrealized 2025 derivative gain, equal to 9.2% of the $78.6 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unrealized mark-to-market gain left in the anchor inflates OE and is capitalized through forecast years and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Gain on commodity derivative instruments for the year ended December 31, 2025 included $7.2 million of mark-to-market gains and $4.9 million of gains on the settlement of commodity derivative instruments compared to $12.2 million of mark-to-market losses and $10.9 million of gains on the settlement of commodity derivative instruments for the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in the $78.6 million anchor is not demonstrated because its exact GAAP-to-OE bridge is missing. The filing separately identifies the unrealized amount, and its Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation removes $7.227 million while retaining settlement economics. If the valuation failed to make the same removal, reducing the anchor proportionately would lower the approximate bear, base and bull values to $5.68, $7.39 and $8.67 per share. That is material to the stated values, although it would reinforce rather than reverse the conclusion that price exceeds modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Produce the exact 2025 GAAP-to-OE bridge and verify removal of the $7.227 million unrealized gain; retain only consistently treated cash settlements and apply the same policy to every historical year.
